h: Seven Shabbos Blessings Unite the Shepherds of Yisrael

p: "These seven of Shabbos — to what do they correspond?
that David said over the waters" (Tehillim 29).
And these are the seven voices of Mattan Torah,
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (בָּבָא קַמָּא יז, א)
in the manner of what they said (Bava Kamma 17a):
which was given with five voices,"
וְכָל הָעָם רוֹאִים אֶת הַקּוֹלוֹת (שְׁמוֹת כ, טו)
'And all the people saw the voices' (Shemos 20:15)?"
and these were before Mattan Torah;
And this is that the first three berachos
corresponds to Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him;
וְהִקְדִּישׁוּ אֶת קְדוֹשׁ יַעֲקֹב (יְשַׁעְיָה כט, כג)
"And they shall sanctify the Holy One of Yaakov" (Yeshayahu 29:23).
And they correspond to the three praises,
"the great, the mighty and the awesome":
who is a chariot for the middah of Gedulah, Chesed;
who is a chariot for the middah of Gevurah;
שֶׁהוּא שְׁלִימוּ דַּאֲבָהָן (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א קנ, א)
who is the completion of the Avos (Zohar I 150a);
that the fear of Hashem Yisbarach
For the middah of "the Fear of Yitzchak"
is that one brings yirah upon himself
שֶׁמֶּלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
that the King of the kings of kings, HaKadosh Baruch Hu,
stands over him and sees his deeds,
and so brings fear upon himself,
like one standing before the king.
And the middah of Yaakov is "awesome":
that is, there falls upon him
וְזֶה עִנְיַן מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (פְּסָחִים פח, א)
And this is the matter of what they said (Pesachim 88a):
"Like Yaakov, who called it a house":
for with him yirah and holiness were permanent.
And the Avos are the root of the words of Torah:
with him began the two thousand years of Torah,
וְקִיֵּים כָּל הַתּוֹרָה עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִיתְּנָה
and he kept the entire Torah before it was given,
אִיתָא בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג פ, ב)
it is stated in the holy Zohar (III 80b):
"The Torah comes from the side of Gevurah";
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר תִּתֵּן אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב (מִיכָה ז, כ)
as it says, "Grant truth to Yaakov" (Michah 7:20),
correspond to Moshe, Aharon and Yosef,
for the middos of Netzach, Hod, Yesod:
Moshe is the groomsman of the King,
Aharon the groomsman of the Queen
for Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
and Aharon, the groomsman of the Queen,
that is, to bring the words of Torah
and Yosef is the aspect of Yesod,
for through him comes the flow
to the middah of Malchus, Knesses Yisrael.
corresponds to the middah of Malchus.
And Shabbos includes all the seven shepherds
for "Shabbos" is the letters Shin, Bas:
the "bas" is crowned with the three Avos
that all agree the Torah was given on Shabbos,
and it was given through Moshe and Aharon;
it is stated in the Zohar Chadash (Toldos)
that it reckons the Mussaf offerings
as corresponding to the seven shepherds,
and reckons the Mussaf of Shabbos as corresponding to Yosef.
And the entire middle berachah of Shabbos
"and grant our portion in Your Torah;
אֵין טוֹב אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה (בְּרָכוֹת ה, א)
and there is no satiety except in words of Torah,
דִּכְתִיב אוֹהֵב כֶּסֶף לֹא יִשְׂבַּע כֶּסֶף (קֹהֶלֶת ה, ט)
as it is written, "One who loves money will not be satisfied with money" (Koheles 5:9);
and although it is expounded in the Gemara (Makkos 10a)
it is expounded about Torah and mitzvos,
that there is no satiety in them,
when there is the revelation of Atika,
from the light "that it was good."
And Shabbos corresponds to the middah of Malchus;
we call her Torah she'b'al peh,"
which is from the primordial light
that was hidden in Torah she'b'al peh.
And this is what it says,
that they correspond to the seven voices
that David said over the waters,
that is, over the words of Torah.
And the psalm speaks of Mattan Torah,
ה׳ עוֹז לְעַמּוֹ יִתֵּן (תְּהִלִּים כט, יא)
"Hashem will give strength to His people" (Tehillim 29:11),
and it is expounded in the Gemara (Zevachim 116a)
about the time of Mattan Torah,
שֶׁנִּתְקַבְּצוּ כּוּלָּם אֵצֶל בִּלְעָם הָרָשָׁע כּוּלֵּי
when they all gathered by the wicked Bilam, etc.:
and He wishes to give it to Yisrael," etc.
And on weekdays we pray eighteen berachos,
corresponding to the eighteen mentions of the Name
in "Give to Hashem, sons of the mighty"
וְהַיְינוּ ג׳ רִאשׁוֹנוֹת כְּנֶגֶד ג׳ הָאָבוֹת
that is, the first three correspond to the three Avos,
correspond to Moshe, Aharon and Yosef, as stated;
that is, each of the tribes
for the middah of Knesses Yisrael
and each one is a separate mention of the Name.
וְזֶה שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ שָׁם)
And this is what is written in the Midrash Rabbah (this parsha there, Bamidbar Rabbah 2:3):
יָרְדוּ עִמּוֹ כ״ב רְבָבוֹת שֶׁל מַלְאָכִים כּוּלֵּי
twenty-two myriads of angels came down with Him, etc.;
they began to long for banners, etc.;
And further on in the Midrash Rabbah:
סִימָנִין הָיוּ לְכָל נָשִׂיא וְנָשִׂיא כּוּלֵּי
for it exists only for that for which it was created;
אֵין מַלְאָךְ אֶחָד עוֹשֶׂה שְׁתֵּי שְׁלִיחוּת
each tribe is distinguished in its own particular holiness.
Nevertheless, the whole of Knesses Yisrael
of all twelve holinesses of the tribes,
"each according to his blessing he blessed them,"
for Yaakov went back and included them together
